title: 12 Cards vs 30: Fixing a Kiosk With Spaced Repetition | vitalii.no
description:
On a family's kiosk display, one child's flashcard deck had only 12 cards while his brothers had 30 - so he ran out and vanished from the wall after about a third of an evening. The zone was also just looping the same fixed lesson cards every five seconds, too fast to think about, with no ladder and no due date tracking whether a card had actually been learned.

The zone was rebuilt to generate cards instead of loop them. Every card shown is now logged and advanced on a real 1-3-10-21 day spaced repetition ladder, capped at one advance per calendar day so a whole evening of TV doesn't count as extra repetition. Norwegian reading gaps that used to be a dead field with no retrievable question now get pulled straight from each child's own finished work. Short decks were topped up so no child runs out early.

The result: card throughput rose about 40 percent per hour once dead reading time was cut, and the child with the shortest deck now keeps pace with his brothers all evening.
